generatedNote: Supported source->target upgrade matrix for every stateful service in docker-compose.yml. Hand-authored source of truth; completeness + pin-drift + schema conformance are gated by scripts/check-upgrade-matrix.mjs (and the vitest suite scripts/ci/__tests__/upgrade-matrix.test.mjs). Human-readable inventory + rationale: docs/internals/architecture/stateful-service-inventory.md. Slice 1 of the upgrade-paths epic (cinatra#1420 / cinatra#1419). This slice defines the DATA; the CLI preflight + `db upgrade-major` (cinatra-cli#128/#129) and the works-after upgrade-from arm (cinatra#1421/#1422) are the consumers.

failClosed.policy: Any (service, from, to) tuple that is not present as a transition with supported=true, and is not a caseException, resolves to UNSUPPORTED. A consumer (cli preflight, db upgrade-major, works-after upgrade-from arm) MUST refuse to proceed on an unsupported tuple — never fall through to a best-effort attempt. An unrecognised source (a deployed version the ledger cannot classify) is likewise unsupported until a transition or case exception is added.

consumptionContract.loader: scripts/lib/upgrade-matrix.mjs (loadUpgradeMatrix / resolveTransition / MATRIX_REVISION). cinatra-cli and the harness vendor or read this same file and resolve transitions through the same fail-closed logic.

consumers.name: cinatra-cli preflight
consumers.uses: deployed-version ledger -> resolveTransition(service, from, to); refuses on unsupported (cinatra-cli#128)

consumers.name: cinatra db upgrade-major
consumers.uses: the supported Postgres transitions + case exceptions to gate the logical dump->fresh-volume->restore (cinatra-cli#129)

consumers.name: works-after upgrade-from arm
consumers.uses: iterates supported stateful transitions to build data-bearing prior-version fixtures that gate a major (cinatra#1422)

consumptionContract.skewRule: Consumers pin the revision they were built against (MATRIX_REVISION) and compare on load. A mismatch is FAIL-CLOSED: the consumer refuses rather than acting on a matrix it was not validated against. schemaVersion MAJOR mismatch is an unparseable-contract hard error. Both sides therefore act on the SAME matrix revision by construction.

services.notes: The platform database, covered by the drizzle migration ledger (packages/migrations). PG 18 moved PGDATA under /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker and requires the volume mounted at the PARENT /var/lib/postgresql; an 18 image refuses a 17-era cluster (fail-closed both directions). Upgrades go through the guarded logical dump->fresh-volume->restore (cinatra db upgrade-major, cinatra-cli#129); pg_dump crosses any source major in one hop, so skipped majors are allowed.

transitions.notes: The SUPPORTED BASELINE transition (cinatra#1417 Case A): the 0.1.9 baseline ships 18, so a 17-era field volume upgrades on the general path — logical dump under 17, restore into a fresh 18 parent-mounted volume. Mount-layout move applies (17 legacy .../data -> 18 parent mount).
Baseline no-op / in-major patch currency; digest re-resolve rides a reviewable pin-diff.
FAIL-CLOSED: PG 19 is prerelease-only at baseline; not validated. Enable only when 19 GAs and its own upgrade lane proves it.

services.notes: Nango's own Postgres. Nango runs its OWN schema migrations at boot; the platform ledger does not cover it. nango-server is therefore a coupled app image: it owns no volume but migrates THIS data dir at boot, so its pin is drift-checked alongside the engine. HELD at 17 (Nango upstream reference compose pins 16, so 17 is already a validated divergence; 18 is unvalidated by upstream). Keeps the legacy .../data mount while <=17. The pre-baseline pg15 nango volume is a case exception (cinatra#1417), not a widening of the general baseline.

transitions.notes: Baseline hold; in-major patch/digest currency only. The pre-baseline pg15 field volume is NOT a general transition — it is the nango-15-to-17 case exception (caseExceptions), so the general baseline stays at 17.
FAIL-CLOSED: unvalidated by Nango upstream; revisit when Nango moves.

services.notes: Twenty CRM's Postgres (profile twenty). Twenty runs its own schema migrations at boot. The Postgres MAJOR is chosen by Twenty upstream; we track upstream, we do not renumber onto the platform major.

transitions.notes: Held at the upstream-dictated major. A Twenty-driven major moves this pin in a reviewable diff and re-runs the upgrade-from proof.

services.notes: Twenty CRM's app local-storage volume (uploads / .local-storage), also mounted by twenty-worker. File-tree state coupled to twenty-db (grouped under family postgres, its coupled engine, like wordpress-files/drupal-files). The image tag is already release-pinned (${TWENTY_TAG:-v2.7.3}, an immutable Twenty release), NOT one of the two floating tags. Twenty runs its own schema migrations at boot; a Twenty app major moves this pin in a reviewable diff.

transitions.notes: Upstream-dictated hold; Twenty performs its own in-place upgrade at boot.

services.notes: Plane's Postgres (profile plane). The Plane app images (backend/live/frontend/space/admin/proxy) run IMPLICIT DB migrations against this data dir at boot (plane-migrator), so they are frozen alongside the engine (coupledAppImages) and were the floating `:stable` tags this slice pinned to v1.3.1 (immutable, digest-bound) via the ${PLANE_TAG:-...} default. Postgres major is Plane-dictated (15.7); we track upstream.

transitions.notes: Held at the Plane-dictated major. A Plane-driven Postgres major moves both this pin AND the coupled app-image pins in one reviewable diff.

services.notes: WordPress database (profile wordpress). WordPress runs its own schema upgrades at boot; the MariaDB engine upgrade is in-place (`mariadb-upgrade` on the same data dir). MariaDB requires SEQUENTIAL major steps (11.4 -> 11.8 -> 12.x); skipping a major is unsupported.

transitions.notes: Baseline hold.

Next in-line minor-LTS hop; in-place data-dir upgrade. Executable guarded path: scripts/upgrade/mariadb-upgrade-major.sh (explicit mariadb-upgrade on a CANDIDATE volume; dump/restore fallback); upgrade-from fixture: scripts/ci/works-after/upgrade-mariadb.sh (cinatra#1421/#1422).
FAIL-CLOSED: MariaDB forbids skipping 11.8 on the way to 12.x. Step through 11.8 first.

services.notes: Drupal database (profile drupal). Drupal runs its own schema updates at boot; the MariaDB engine upgrade is in-place and sequential-major (same rule as wordpress-mariadb).

transitions.notes: Baseline hold.

Next in-line hop; same executable guarded path + fixture as wordpress-mariadb (one family path, both services): scripts/upgrade/mariadb-upgrade-major.sh + scripts/ci/works-after/upgrade-mariadb.sh (cinatra#1421/#1422).
FAIL-CLOSED: sequential-only; step through 11.8.

services.notes: The WordPress content root (/var/www/html): uploads + installed plugins/themes (the cinatra plugin is bind-mounted separately). File-tree state, not a DB engine; a WordPress core/PHP major re-runs WP's own DB upgrade against wordpress-db and rewrites the content tree in place (no engine dump/restore). The `family: mariadb` tag groups it with its coupled DB; classified object-store because the durable state is the uploads tree.

transitions.notes: Baseline hold. WP 6.9 / 7.0 + php 8.5 each ride their own reviewable image-tag bump; WP performs its own in-place content/schema upgrade at boot.

services.notes: The Drupal site files dir (web/sites/default): settings + the public files/uploads tree. Locally-built image (docker/drupal). Durable state is the files tree; Drupal runs its own DB updates against drupal-db at boot. Classified object-store for the same reason as wordpress-files. baselinePin.image is the build marker (not a registry tag) since this is a local build; pin-drift for it is out of scope (no floating registry tag).

transitions.notes: Locally built; a Drupal/PHP major rebuilds the image and Drupal runs its own update.php-equivalent at boot.

services.notes: The knowledge graph store (graphiti-coupled). A Neo4j major is an ONE-WAY in-place store-format upgrade performed by the server on first start (NOT a pg_upgrade-style dump/restore). RPO floor: take a `neo4j-admin database dump` BEFORE rolling the pin in an environment with a populated store — a rollback needs the pre-upgrade dump because an old binary cannot open a new-format store. Downgrade unsupported. Neo4j retired the 5.x semver line at 5.26 and moved to CalVer; the CalVer line is the 5.x successor (linear).

transitions.notes: The applied semver->CalVer hop. In-place store-format upgrade on first start; monthly dump is the rollback RPO floor.
Baseline hold; a CalVer digest re-resolve (same tag, republished bytes) rides its own pin-diff, gated by the graphiti works-after round-trip.

services.notes: DERIVED state (owns NO volume — the graph lives in Neo4j). knowledge-graph-mcp fronts Neo4j over MCP and re-projects/extracts into it. An upgrade is a repin + rebuild (re-project from source), no backup/RPO of its own; coupled to the neo4j pin. Listed in the matrix as an explicit volume-less entry so the family is covered and a future major re-enters the lane paired with neo4j.

transitions.notes: At newest stable upstream; only change is a digest re-pin. A published knowledge-graph-mcp major re-pairs with neo4j and re-runs the works-after round-trip.

services.notes: BullMQ cache/queue backend. The volume holds regenerable cache/queue state, so the fail-safe upgrade path is discard-recreate. Forward RDB is readable (7 -> 8 upgrade in place is fine); DOWNGRADE is unsafe — Redis 8 writes RDB v14 which Redis 7 refuses (crash-loop), so a downgrade requires CLEARING the dump first (documented downgrade path).

transitions.notes: Applied major. Forward RDB is compatible; the works-after redis arm proves a real bullmq enqueue->run->complete round-trip on 8. Data-preserving guarded superset of discard-recreate for a still-populated 7-era volume: scripts/upgrade/redis-upgrade-major.sh (AOF explicit); upgrade-from fixture: scripts/ci/works-after/upgrade-redis.sh (cinatra#1421/#1422).
Baseline hold.
FAIL-CLOSED downgrade: clear the RDB dump first (regenerable cache/queue state), then recreate on 7. scripts/upgrade/redis-upgrade-major.sh refuses this hop at resolve time (cinatra#1421).

services.notes: Twenty's Redis (profile twenty). No named volume (ephemeral cache/queue). Upstream-dictated major; discard-recreate on any bump.

transitions.notes: Upstream-dictated hold. Ephemeral cache -> a bump just recreates.

services.notes: Plane's Valkey (profile plane). Cache/queue for Plane; Plane-dictated. Valkey RDB/AOF is downgrade-unsafe like Redis, but the state is regenerable, so discard-recreate is the fail-safe path.

transitions.notes: Plane-dictated hold. A Plane-driven Valkey major moves this pin in a reviewable diff; cache is discard-recreate.

services.notes: Plane's RabbitMQ (profile plane). Queue state is drainable, so discard-recreate is the fail-safe path. The 3.x -> 4.x hop is FEATURE-FLAG-GATED: ALL stable feature flags must be enabled on 3.13 BEFORE the 4.0 jump (4.0 requires them and refuses to boot otherwise). Skipping through the flag graph (e.g. 3.12 -> 4.0 without enabling 3.13's flags) is unsupported.

transitions.notes: Plane-dictated hold.
FAIL-CLOSED until the feature-flag hop is enabled+proven: enable ALL stable 3.13 feature flags first, then jump. Drain-and-recreate is the operational fallback (queue state is regenerable).

services.notes: Plane's object store for uploads. FROZEN this slice from the floating `:latest` to the immutable dated release RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (digest-bound). Object-store data must be PRESERVED across an upgrade (in-place; MinIO rolls forward the same erasure/single-drive server line). KNOWN-UNKNOWN: an existing `latest` volume has an unrecorded last-writer release — the deployed-version ledger (cinatra-cli#128) records the running release at preflight; until it does, an unclassified source is fail-closed. A release that dropped the legacy fs-mode/gateway is a hard boundary (the pinned line is already the current server, so no boundary is crossed by holding).

transitions.notes: Baseline hold. A dated-release bump rides a reviewable pin-diff; object data rolls forward in place.
FAIL-CLOSED: an existing `:latest` volume whose writer release is unknown must be classified by the preflight ledger before an upgrade is attempted.

services.notes: Dev npm registry (package storage). Ephemeral dev cache of published extension tarballs; discard-recreate on any bump (re-publish repopulates it). 6.7.4 is the latest stable line; 7 is prerelease-only, so no major is offered.

transitions.notes: Baseline hold; digest-pinned. A future 7 major re-enters its own lane.

caseExceptions.notes: The pre-baseline pg15 nango volume (older existing install). Supported for this concrete case only (skips 16 in one logical dump/restore hop); does NOT widen the general nango baseline, which holds at 17.
